newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds widen over rallying Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds widen over rallying Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities widened modestly to Treasuries on Friday.
"We were tighter for a while this morning, but then the Treasury market exploded," a Ginnie Mae trader said.

Treasuries rallied after a report issued Friday morning showed that Gross Domestic Product grew at a strong 4.7 percent rate in the fourth quarter of 1996, but that the surge did not appear to increase inflation pressures.
Pass-throughs attracted plenty of buyers, though, particularly funds, traders said.
Commercial mortgages traded more slowly, however, one expert in that market said. New supply has been slow in coming over the past few days, helping to preserve prices, he said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 10/32 at 100-08/32, yielding 100 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were up 11/32 at 100-04/32 and 100-09/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 17/32 at 99-29/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
